description: Extractors are applied on every message that is received by this input. Use them to extract and transform any text data into fields that allow you easy filtering and analysis later on. Example: Extract the HTTP response code from a log message, transform it to a numeric field and attach it as {{field}} to the message.

list_item.subtitle_copy: Trying to extract data from {{source}} into {{target}}, leaving the original intact.
list_item.subtitle_cut: Trying to extract data from {{source}} into {{target}}, not leaving the original intact.
list_item.condition_string: Will only attempt to run if the message includes the string {{value}}
list_item.condition_regex: Will only attempt to run if the message matches the regular expression {{value}}

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.no_messages: No message passed through here yet.

edit.condition_string_help: Type a string that the field should contain in order to attempt the extraction.
edit.condition_regex_help: Type a regular expression that the field should contain in order to attempt the extraction.
edit.condition_matches: Matches! Extractor would run against this example.
edit.condition_no_match: Does not match! Extractor would not run.
edit.condition_type_help: Extracting only from messages that match a certain condition helps you avoiding wrong or unnecessary extractions and can also save CPU resources.
edit.cursor_strategy_help: Do you want to copy or cut from source? You cannot use the cutting feature on standard fields like message and source.
edit.target_field_help: Choose a field name to store the extracted value. It can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores. Example: http_response_code.
edit.condition_string: Only attempt extraction if field contains string
edit.condition_regex: Only attempt extraction if field matches regular expression
edit.title: Extractor title
edit.title_help: A descriptive name for this extractor.
